# 1 Epidemiological highlights

— 31 new confirmed cases (Ituri 27, Nord-Kivu 4) and 10 notified deaths, of which 7 community deaths in Ituri — Bunia 3, Lita 2, Rwampara 1, Fataki 1 — and 3 in Nord-Kivu (Katwa, Butembo).

— Ituri accounts for 27 of the 31 new cases and all of the day's community deaths; transmission remains sustained in the Djugu–Irumu corridor (Bunia, Lita, Nizi, Rwampara).

— Tshopo (Kisangani — Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo and Lubunga ZS; 4 cases / 2 deaths) and Haut-Uélé (Wamba: 7 confirmed cases, all deceased, originating from Nia-Nia) remain linked to the Ituri epicentre; the Kisangani cases all originate from the Nia-Nia health zone (Ituri).
No new health zone notified on 12 July, with the national total remaining at 42 ZS out of 140.

— Sud-Kivu — 47 consecutive days without a new confirmed case (as of 12 July 2026), or more than twice the maximum incubation period: the province maintains residual surveillance with a view to declaring the end of the outbreak.

— Fifteen (15) patients declared recovered (Ituri 13, Nord-Kivu 2 at the Beni CTE (Ebola treatment centre)).
Deployment of 3 additional EDS teams to Nizi (6 in total) in response to community mortality.

— Points of entry / points of control: 71/71 PoC activated and PoE reinforced (100 %); 144 094 travellers screened (Ituri + Nord-Kivu); 7 alerts notified, 2 live alerts validated and referred and 4 dead bodies intercepted.
Activation of PoC Makoko 2 (Mambasa) and partial opening of PoE Ruzizi I and II (Sud-Kivu).

— Cumulative: 1 963 confirmed cases and 718 deaths — case fatality rate of 36,6 % — in 42 health zones out of 140 (5 provinces); progression since SitRep No. 058: +31 cases and +10 deaths.

At the end of the day of 12 July 2026, no new health zone has been notified; the national cumulative total remains at 42 health zones out of 140 distributed across 5 provinces (Ituri 26/36, Nord-Kivu 11/34, Tshopo 3/23 including Lubunga).
As of 12 July 2026, Sud-Kivu totals 47 consecutive days without a new confirmed case (more than twice the maximum incubation period), which paves the way for the declaration of the end of the outbreak in the province, subject to residual epidemiological vigilance.

Provincial dynamics and concentration of cases
Approximately 90,5 % of cases (n=1 772) and 85,4 % of deaths (n=608) are concentrated in Ituri, which remains the epicentre of the outbreak (crude case fatality rate 34,3 %).
The zones of Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nizi and Nyankunde account for the majority of the province's cases.
On 12 July, Bunia (11 cases), Lita (6) and Nizi (5) accounted for the new cases, and all 7 deaths of the day occurred in the community.
Mongbwalu displays the most marked severity (52,0 %, or 171 deaths for 329 cases), mainly linked to the substantial proportion of community deaths.

Geographical spread — Haut-Uélé and Tshopo
Tshopo has three affected health zones — Makiso-Kisangani, Mangobo and Lubunga (Kisangani; provincial cumulative total: 4 cases, 2 deaths) — alongside Haut-Uélé (Wamba ZS: 7 cases, 7 deaths, all originating from Nia-Nia).
No new cases were notified there on 12 July.
All these cases are linked to the Ituri epicentre (Nia-Nia / PK51) and do not constitute indigenous transmission.
The city of Kisangani (≈ 1,6 million inhabitants) nevertheless increases the risk of urban, riverine and air diffusion.
Interventions have however been strengthened there — surveillance, safe and dignified burial teams, isolation and case management capacities.

▍ 2.5 — Demographic characteristics

The population pyramid shows a predominance of working-age adults: the 20–29 and 30–39 age groups account for the majority of confirmed cases, with more women than men in the 20–29 age group.
Investigations into these differences are ongoing; they could reflect differences in risk exposure (for example among caregivers).
Children under 10 years of age and elderly people are proportionately less affected, a profile consistent with transmission linked to community, occupational and caregiving activities.

The alert rate remains proportionately low in Ituri, as shown by a much higher positivity than in Nord-Kivu.

▍ 3.2 — Laboratory: tests and positivity

— Ituri: 203 samples analysed (189 blood, 14 swab) — 27 positive (positivity 13,3 %): Bunia 11, Lita 6, Nizi 5, Rwampara 3, Fataki 1, Drodro 1.

— Nord-Kivu: 99 samples analysed — 6 positive (positivity 6,1 %), concentrated in Butembo (Beni 0).

— Sud-Kivu: 8 samples received this day (cumulative 231 analysed, positivity 1,3 %); no new positive results.

In Ituri, 203 samples were analysed for a positivity of 13,3 % — declining despite sustained volume; Nord-Kivu retains a low yield (6,1 %) and the backlog of samples remains to be cleared.

405 new contacts listed in Ituri and 164 in Nord-Kivu; 8 contacts became suspects in Ituri (12 in Nord-Kivu) and 364 completed their 21-day follow-up.
Six zones (Gethy, Lolwa, Mandima, Logo, Rimba, Kambala) did not submit their report in Ituri.
In Sud-Kivu, 226 contacts under follow-up, of which 2 became positive.
By hotspot zone, follow-up varies widely: Bunia 96,9 %, Nizi 92,6 %, Mongbwalu 89,0 %, Rwampara 85,2 %, but drops to Nyankunde 28,9 %, Nia-Nia 36,2 % and Kilo 44,0 %.
As of 12 July, none of the 27 new confirmed cases in Ituri was a previously listed contact (0 %): virtually all cases occur outside known transmission chains.
On the cumulative total, the proportion of cases linked to a registered contact remains low (≈ 15–20 %).
Among documented contacts, neighbour and family relationships predominate.
Analysis by circumstance shows that exposure at home (household) mainly involves family links, whereas contacts in hospital, funeral and occupational settings present a high proportion of "unknown" relationships — profiles at risk of extra-household transmission.

# 4 Points of entry and points of control (PoE/PoC)

The 71 points of control (PoC) and points of entry (PoE) in epidemic zones remain 100 % activated and reinforced (Ituri 57, Nord-Kivu 14).
As of 12 July, 144 094 travellers were screened in Ituri and Nord-Kivu (screening 95,4 %, awareness raising 98,1 %).
Seven (7) alerts notified — 2 live alerts validated and referred to the CT/CTE and 4 dead bodies intercepted.

▍ 4.1 — Alerts at crossing points (24 h)

Ituri — 5 alerts (3 live, 2 dead bodies)
Two live alerts validated, isolated and referred: at PoC Nyamusasi, a 26-year-old man (Tchomia→Kasenyi, fever), transferred to the CT; at PoC Banguba, a 32-year-old woman (PK51/Nia-Nia, fever, vomiting, headache), transferred to the CTE.
One alert (PoC Marabo, 16-year-old boy, Beni→Hoho) invalidated after reassessment.
Two dead bodies intercepted — PoC Nyori (swabbed) and PoC Route Watsa (awaiting EDS).
Of note: activation of PoC Makoko 2 (Mambasa ZS).

Nord-Kivu — 2 alerts (2 dead bodies)
Two dead bodies intercepted and transported for sampling: at PoC Mukulia, a 60-year-old man (Biakato→Butembo), directed to the morgue of HGR Beni; and at the Mususa PoC (Musienene ZS), a 79-year-old woman (Butembo→Mbau).
No live alert validated in Nord-Kivu this day.

Sud-Kivu — 5 alerts (all live) · preparedness mechanism
Five alerts notified at PoC Kazingo and Ihusi — 3 validated and placed at the UOB transit centre, 2 invalidated.
Partial opening of PoE Ruzizi I and Ruzizi II.
Over the period from 22 June to 12 July, 49 187 travellers crossed the PoE (including 1 317 in international traffic) and 637 319 the PoC; 100 % of the province's PoC/PoE remain activated (68 082 people screened as of 12/07).

# 5 Response activities by pillar — summary of 12 July

COORDINATION
Meetings with partners (PTF) and field supervisions.
Advocacy by the Minister of Health with Ituri leaders: announcement of 10 ambulances and health/bank cards to secure payment of staff; commitment of provincial deputies.

PCI / WASH
Ituri: 42/67 transient households decontaminated in 48 h; 12/12 ESS of confirmed cases decontaminated; 924/1 640 providers trained.
Nord-Kivu: decontamination of the morgue and ESS (Beni, Katwa, Kalunguta); 18 ESS evaluated (score < 50 %); 15 providers trained (Beni).

SAFE AND DIGNIFIED BURIALS (EDS)
Ituri: deployment of 3 additional teams to Nizi (6 in total); execution of EDS and swabs; stockout of supplies reported in Nizi.
Nord-Kivu: 36 death alerts, 35 bodies swabbed and secured, 29 EDS performed.

HOLISTIC CASE MANAGEMENT (PECH)
15 newly recovered (Ituri 13, Nord-Kivu 2); 8 ambulance runs (3 operational, 2 broken down); 987 hot meals served; 2 suspected cases having left isolation before results (Ituri).
Mental health (SMSPS (mental health and psychosocial support)): see Table 8.

COMMUNICATION (RCCE / CREC)
Ituri: discharge ceremony for recovered patients; commitment of provincial deputies; 1 265 people reached in home visits.
Nord-Kivu: community dialogues (Katwa, Beni, Butembo, Mabalako); 7 836 households visited; 25 398 people reached door-to-door; 30/34 radio stations broadcasting.

CONTINUITY OF ESSENTIAL SERVICES (CSSE)
Elaboration of the response plan; mapping of partners offering free healthcare (18/36 ZS in Ituri); follow-up of affected frontline personnel (see Table 9).

RESEARCH, INNOVATION & VACCINATION
EBO-PEP clinical trials (ALIMA) in preparation; inter-partner meeting on 13/07 (INRB, ALIMA, OMS).

LOGISTICS
Nord-Kivu: team deployment; delivery of PCI (infection prevention and control) kits and medicines (Mambangu Military Hospital); repair of mobile vehicle 103 (Mutsora).
Ituri: support for the transport of supplies and deployment of pillars.

SECURITY
No new major incidents reported on 12 July; heightened vigilance around PoE/PoC and care facilities; coordination maintained for access to at-risk zones.

NUTRITION
Sud-Kivu: distribution of hot rations to cases in isolation (Fomulac, Lwiro).
Ituri: 16 specific diets and hot meals served (creche, companions, frontline staff).

PREVENTION OF SEXUAL EXPLOITATION AND ABUSE (PSEA / PRSEAH)
Sud-Kivu: transmission of the SITREP to the PEAS network; SEA awareness raising for RECO (community health worker) and the community; 50 providers briefed and signatories of codes of conduct; popularisation of zero tolerance and the toll-free number (495555 / 151).
Ituri: cumulative total of 2 250 people briefed, coverage extended to 5 health zones.

# 6 Main challenges, impacts and required actions


| No. | Challenges | Impact | Required actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs) and community resistance | Confirmation delay, underestimation of cases, high community mortality | Intensify CREC, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, reinforce EDS teams (done: +3 in Nizi) |
| 2 | Insufficient CTE/CT capacity; saturation in Nord-Kivu (117,2 %) | Admission delays, risk of nosocomial transmission | Accelerate CTE expansion, deploy temporary structures, open more transit centres |
| 3 | Contact tracing below target (81,5 % vs 95 %) and heterogeneous (Nyankunde 28,9 %, Nia-Nia 36,2 %) | Unbroken transmission chains | Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO); reinforced supervision |
| 4 | Low alert reporting and investigation in Ituri; ZS / DHIS2 discrepancies | Undetected transmission, silent spread | Reinforce community surveillance; harmonise ZS/DHIS2 databases; add investigators |
| 5 | None of the new cases linked to a listed contact (0 % on 12/07) | Uncontrolled community transmission | In-depth investigation, active case finding, expansion of listing |
| 6 | Insufficient ambulances and isolation structures | Delays in transfer and isolation | Pre-position ambulances (including at PoE/PoC), deploy CTs in each ZS |
| 7 | Sample backlog and delayed diagnosis in Nord-Kivu | Confirmation delay, high case fatality rate (56,5 %) | Laboratory catch-up plan, reinforcement of diagnostic capacities |
| 8 | Frontline personnel infected (114 cases, 36 deaths, case fatality rate 31,6 %) | Loss of capacity and nosocomial risk | Reinforce PCI, supply PPE and PCI/WASH kits |
| 9 | Insecurity and limited access (Nia-Nia, CODECO/ADF) | Restriction of operations | Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access |
| 10 | High population mobility and urban extension (Tshopo/Kisangani) | Risk of urban, riverine and cross-border spread | Reinforce surveillance at PoE/PoC and cross-border coordination |
| 11 | Insufficient resources: mobility and payment of providers | Demotivation of actors, inefficiency | Mobilise resources, regularise payments |
| 12 | Continuity of essential services compromised; insufficient essential generic drugs and nutritional supplies | Increase in indirect mortality (non-Ebola) | Make free healthcare effective; supply essential generic drugs and nutritional supplies |
